description: From the 2026-08-20 cold review: first_rejected_mutation decodes and walks every mutation of every commit inside the GenServer accept loop - a second full decode pass on the proxy's one serialized resource (finalization decodes again in the task). Proposal (pending FDB design audit): move the scan into the batch pipeline with per-transaction rejection through the existing reply machinery, batch continues - FDB precedent is validateAndProcessTenantAccess doing per-tx sendError inside postResolution rather than at accept. Accepted cost: a rejected transaction's batch still consumes a commit version. Audit to confirm placement (before resolution vs at conflict-section extraction), interaction with abort accounting, and what FDB actually does if a client bypasses getMaxWriteKey.

comments.text: FDB design audit CONFIRMED with refinements. (1) Per-tx rejection inside batch processing is FDB's own shape: validateAndProcessTenantAccess does reply.sendError + committed[t]=TenantFailure and the batch proceeds (CommitProxyServer.actor.cpp:1757-1792); final reply loop skips answered txs (:2754-2757). (2) FDB's accept-vs-pipeline criterion: byte-pure request checks at accept (even full scans - verifyTenantPrefix :318-392), versioned-state checks in-pipeline; Bedrock's decode cost model favors pipeline placement for the bounds scan. (3) FDB is genuinely unguarded against dishonest clients: key past 0xFFFF gets EMPTY tags via keyInfo sentinel (RangeMap.h:135-141, commented-out assert :111) -> silently dropped by every storage server; out-of-range conflict range -> ASSERT(resolvers.size()) proxy CRASH (:180); atomic on system keys -> silent txnStateStore/keyspace divergence. Our proxy-side enforcement guards real holes - keep it, move it. PLACEMENT: run first_rejected_mutation during the existing extraction pass in resolve_conflicts (finalization.ex:335-343/:393-402) before resolver calls; on rejection reply_fn immediately, send EMPTY conflict sections + [] metadata to keep resolver indices stable (FDB creates out-transactions on all resolvers for alignment :260-265; and unlike FDB we avoid polluting conflict history with rejected txs' ranges); union rejected into replied_indices; keep binary/mode guards at accept. Rejection must stay a pure function of transaction bytes.

title: Move proxy keyspace validation off the serialized accept loop
